Annex H

(informative)

Regional information

## H.1 General

This annex contains additional requirements for fixed steel offshore structures applicable to particular geographical regions (which can form all or part of the offshore waters of one or more countries) because of their environments or local customs and practices. The information in this annex is applicable for structures located in the defined areas and informative for other regions. The contents have been developed by subject experts from the region concerned to supplement the provisions of this document. This annex contains some regional and national data, including regional environmental conditions and local design, construction and operating practices. The regulatory framework is explained, but neither regulatory requirements nor reference to specific legislation is included.

## H.2 North West Europe,,,`,`,,

H.2.1 Description of region, ```,,,

The North West Europe waters are diverse and stretch from the sub-Arctic waters off Norway and Iceland to the Atlantic seaboard of France and Ireland in the south. Clause H.2 specifically includes the waters of the following countries:

— United Kingdom;   
— Ireland;   
— Norway;   
— Germany (North Sea and Baltic Sea);   
— Denmark (North Sea and Baltic Sea);   
— The Netherlands;   
— Belgium;   
— France (Atlantic seaboard only);   
— Spain (Atlantic seaboard only).

H.2.2 Regulatory framework in North West Europe

H.2.2.1 General

The European Union (EU) countries and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries which border the offshore area are linked in the European Economic Area (EEA). Regional requirements are made by the EU. EU requirements are implemented by each of the EU member states through their own law-making process. Under the EEA agreement, EFTA countries comply with the requirements of

directives and other regulatory requirements agreed upon by the EU, which includes directives relating to safety and lifting of trade barriers.

H.2.2.2 UK regulatory framework

The UK regulatory framework for oil and gas development is based on a goal setting regime with no detailed technical provisions. It is the responsibility of the duty holder, who is normally the owner, to determine the technical requirements by reference to international standards, codes of practice or other means.

H.2.2.3 Norwegian regulatory framework

The Norwegian Pollution Control Authority, the Norwegian Social and Health Directorate and the Petroleum Safety Authority (former NPD) have made joint regulations related to health, safety and the environment on the Norwegian continental shelf. The regulations are the framework regulations (Royal Decree), the management regulations, the information duty regulations, the facilities regulations and the activities regulations. Guidelines to the regulations have been prepared. The guidelines give references to acceptable standards, codes of practice and other documents.

H.2.2.4 Danish regulatory framework

The Danish Energy Authority is the supervising authority of health and safety. Issues concerning emissions to the environment are handled by the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, while other environmental issues lie with the Danish Energy Authority.

It is the responsibility of the duty holder to ensure that the health and safety level is satisfactory and documented in accordance with the “Act on Safety etc. on Offshore Installations for Exploration, Production and Transportation of Hydrocarbons (The Offshore Safety Act)”.

H.2.2.5 Dutch regulatory framework

The Dutch regulatory framework for oil and gas development is based on a goal setting regime with no detailed technical provisions. It is the responsibility of the duty holder to determine the technical requirements by reference to international standards, codes of practice or other means.

H.2.3 Technical information for North West Europe

H.2.3.1 Minimum RSR

The minimum RSR for a conventionally framed L1 jacket structure shall be 1,85 (see 7.11.1).

For non-conventionally framed structures, see A.7.11.1.3.

H.2.3.2 Partial action factor

If the option given in H.2.3.1 is not adopted, the partial action factor for metocean actions shall be 1,35 (see 9.10), unless a rational analysis demonstrates an alternative value is appropriate.

## H.3 Canada

H.3.1 Description of region

The geographical basis for this subclause is the region bounded by the continental shelf margins of Canada. The region encompasses both shallow water and deepwater areas of offshore Canada that are either ice-free regions (Pacific Ocean off the west coast of British Columbia) or regions that may be subjected seasonally to the presence of sea ice and icebergs. Sea ice can be present in the Beaufort Sea, Offshore the Arctic Islands, Baffin Bay, Davis Strait, offshore Newfoundland and Labrador, in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, as well as offshore Nova Scotia, although the occurrence of sea ice in the offshore Nova Scotia area is rare. Icebergs are typically encountered in the waters on the north and east coasts of offshore Newfoundland and Labrador.

H.3.2 Regulatory framework in Canada

Oil and gas exploration and production activities in Canada’s non-Accord Frontier Lands (defined as the Nunavut Territories, Sable Island and its submarine areas, and areas not within a province adjacent to the coast of Canada, to the outer edge of the continental margin or to a distance of two hundred nautical miles, whichever is greater, but excluding the offshore areas of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador) are governed by the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act [H.1] and the Canada Petroleum Resources Act [H.2]. The Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act and certain elements of the Canada Petroleum Resources Act are administered by the Canadian Energy Regulator (CER) () in all of the non-Accord Frontier Lands.

Oil and gas exploration and production activities in Canada’s Accord Frontier Lands (defined as offshore areas in the Canada Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act (CNSOPRAIA [H.3]) and the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act (C-NLAAIA [H.4]) are governed by the CNSOPRAIA and C-NLAAIA and mirror the provincial Accord Implementation Acts, respectively. The provincial acts are the Canada Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation (Nova Scotia) Act [H.5] and the Canada Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Newfoundland and Labrador Act [H.6], respectively. These acts are administered by joint federal-provincial offshore petroleum boards. In the Nova Scotia Offshore Accord area, the regulator is the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Board (CNSOPB), and in the Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Accord area the regulator is the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board (C-NLOPB).

For the offshore areas, the three boards (CER, CNSOPB, and C-NLOPB) are responsible for, amongst other things, the regulation of oil and gas exploration and production work or activities including:

— issuance of licences for offshore exploration and development (CNSOPB and C-NLOPB only);   
— issuance of authorization and approvals for exploration and production work or activity pursuant to the operative statute and its regulations;   
— health and safety of workers;   
— protection of the environment during petroleum activities;   
— management and conservation of petroleum resources;   
— compliance with the provisions of the laws dealing with employment and industrial benefits by the offshore petroleum board in the Accord areas, and for Canada Benefits by the Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs for non-Accord Frontier Lands generally north of 60° north,

and by the Department of Natural Resources for non-Accord Frontier lands generally south of 60° north;

— resource evaluation and data collection, curation and distribution.

H.3.3 Technical information for Canada

H.3.3.1 Partial action factors

The partial action factor for metocean actions shall be 1,35 for L1 structures (see 9.10), unless rational analysis demonstrates that an alternative value is appropriate.

H.3.3.2 Materials – DC approach – SQL V

ISO 19902:2007 permitted steels with no CVN impact testing requirement to be used for structural components to DC 5 classification – see Table 19.6-1. Prior to the adoption in Canada of ISO 19902, CAN/CSA S473 also permitted the use of steels without CVN impact testing in the least stringent design categories.

Based on a history of successful use in Canada, weldable grade structural steels that do not require CVN impact testing may be used under the following conditions:

— SMYS ≤ 355 MPa   
— maximum thickness of 25mm   
— structural components assigned to DC 5 classification

For application of the requirements of H.3.3.3, in line with the classifications and categories listed in Tables 19.6-2 and 19.6-3, steel of this quality can be treated as a “SQL V category” steel.

H.3.3.3 Welding

H.3.3.3.1 DC approach

In this document, SQL IV steels are permitted for use in structural steel components classified as DC 5 (19.6.3.2). However, SQL IV steels are not permitted for use for LAST lower than -10°C (F.1). Accordingly, no corresponding weld or HAZ toughness requirements are included in Table F.1.

Based on a history of successful use in Canada, DC 5 classified steel components constructed of SQL IV steel may be used for LAST below -10°C. CVN impact testing of the weld and HAZ shall be required. The test temperature shall be equal to or below the test temperature for SQL IV required in Table 19.6-3. The minimum CVN impact energy requirement shall be 27 J.

Similarly, based on a history of successful use in Canada, DC 5 classified steel components constructed of SQL V steel (H.3.3.2) may be used for LAST below -10°C. CVN impact testing of the weld and HAZ shall not be required provided CVN impact tested filler metals/weld consumables are used that have a minimum CVN impact energy of 27 J at the LAST.

H.3.3.3.2 Welding standard

If the welding standard selected for use is CSA W59 [H.9], the following requirements shall apply to accommodate the changes to material toughness introduced in this document.

CSA W59 Annex U refers to toughness classes in terms of NT, CV1, CV2, CV2Z, CV2X, and CV2ZX as applied to both the MC and DC approaches in ISO 19902:2007. With this document, toughness for the DC approach is now defined in terms of SQL I, II, III, and IV (19.6.3.2), as well as SQL V (H.3.3.2).

General requirements and references in CSA W59 Annex U concerning CV1 and CV2 steels (with impact testing) shall also apply to SQL I, II, III, and IV steels. General requirements and references in CSA W59 Annex U concerning NT steels shall apply to SQL V steels.

When evaluating welding procedure qualifications for use on MC or DC steels, the requirements for toughness (CVN or CTOD) for the MC approach (Annex E ) or for the DC approach (Annex F and H.3.3.3.1) shall be met. The range of qualification defined by either of these approaches shall be in accordance with the additional essential variables for CVN impact testing (20.2.2.4.2) and for CTOD testing (20.2.2.5.4), and the general requirements of CSA W59 Annex U.

When performing qualification testing, fabricators should take into account the weld metal and HAZ CVN toughness requirements for both the MC and DC approaches. Testing at the lowest temperature and meeting the higher absorbed energy requirements should maximize the qualification range and reduce the number of qualifications required. Fabricators should also consider utilizing the steel manufacturer’s CTOD pre-qualification results for base steel and HAZ to avoid CTOD testing of the HAZ during weld procedure qualifications.

H.3.3.3.3 Fabrication contractor, inspection contractor, and personnel qualifications

If the welding standard selected for use is CSA W59, the qualification requirements provided in Annex U of CSA W59 shall apply [H.9].

When CSA W59 is not the welding standard selected for use, the owner shall ensure that the following subject areas are addressed by the selected welding standards or by project specifications:

a) Welding fabrication company [H.8]:

1) qualified welding engineering personnel;   
2) qualified welding supervisory personnel;   
3) documented, qualified and approved welders and welding operators with regular validation of qualifications;   
4) documented, qualified, and approved welding procedures.

b) Welding inspection company [H.10]:

1) documented, qualified, and approved welding inspection/NDT procedures for methods used and products inspected, including special practices for tubular TKY connections, when applicable;   
2) qualified welding inspection/NDT supervisory personnel;   
3) documented qualified welding inspection/NDT personnel with regular validation of qualification, including special qualifications for TKY connections, when applicable.

c) Welding inspectors qualified on the basis of training, experience and examination in the method used and products inspected, including tubular TKY connections, when applicable [H.11].

The above qualifications for items a), b), and c) shall be recognized as being equivalent to those referenced in CSA W59, Annex U [H.9].

The services of a recognized independent third party organization can be considered to verify ongoing compliance with these requirements.
